_comment: a.js and b.js are one import cycle, and a.js runs first. Node runs barrel.js, then ready.js, then the cycle. other.js is a second entry, so a.js and b.js go to a shared chunk, which main.js imports before the code of ready.js. With `preserveModules`, main.js imports b.js, the owner of `f`, before barrel.js. In both outputs a.js runs before ready.js. The early calls in a.js run only when `ready` is not set, so they do not run in Node. They must not throw in the output: the calls of `f` from b.js and the guarded call of `later` before its declaration in a.js. In Node, the call of `f` in the first `try` block does not run, because the code before it throws. The call of `later` in the argument of `gate` does not run in Node either, because the getter of `gate` throws first. The other call of `later` throws in Node too, but it must not make the guarded call throw.
